AfterAddedToRoom.rationale: SHARED-FINDINGS section 2, copied verbatim in substance: the sim has no add-to-room phase -- creature creation IS construction -- so AfterAddedToRoom's effect is applied from __init__ (bowlbugs.py:42-47). The game runs it from MonsterModel.AfterAddedToRoom awaited by CombatManager.AfterCreatureAdded (CombatManager.cs:860-867) inside StartCombatInternal (CombatManager.cs:393-398), i.e. after every creature is on the board and before Hook.BeforeCombatStart. Same observable today on all three of section 2's clauses (listener set / HP-roll inversion / roll ordering); the concrete trigger that would make it a gap is a relic, potion or power listening on modify_power_amount / on_power_applied / modify_block_* without gating on the player, or a starting power whose amount reads owner.max_hp. Rule 7: the four relic files and sts2_rl/powers.py that section 2's clause (a)/(b) argument cites are NOT hashed by this record. Here the effect is PowerCmd.Apply<ImbalancedPower>(Creature, 1m, Creature) (BowlbugRock.cs:63-67) -> PowerCmd.apply(hooks, self, ImbalancedPower, 1). Self-applied, no card, literal amount. Note the sim sets `self.is_off_balance = False` BEFORE super().__init__ (bowlbugs.py:43) because build_machine's conditional branch reads it, matching C#'s field initialiser (BowlbugRock.cs:26).

GenerateMoveStateMachine.rationale: Node-by-node identical to BowlbugRock.cs:69-82: HEADBUTT_MOVE -> ConditionalBranchState 'POST_HEADBUTT', DIZZY_MOVE -> HEADBUTT_MOVE, initial HEADBUTT_MOVE. Branch add order matches and is observable (first true condition wins, ConditionalBranchState.cs:44-54): `AddState(DIZZY, () => IsOffBalance)` then `AddState(HEADBUTT, () => !IsOffBalance)` vs add_state(dizzy, ...) then add_state(headbutt, ...) (bowlbugs.py:56-57). Executed (monster_probes_b04.py graphs).

guards.what: the dizzy turn is delivered by the DIZZY_MOVE state instead of by CreatureCmd.Stun's synthetic STUNNED move
guards.rationale: C# reaches the lost turn twice over: ImbalancedPower.AfterDamageGiven sets `bowlbugRock.IsOffBalance = true` when the owner's attack WasFullyBlocked (ImbalancedPower.cs:18-33), and then HeadbuttMove itself, still executing, does `if (IsOffBalance) await Stun()` -> CreatureCmd.Stun(Creature, DizzyMove) (BowlbugRock.cs:84-101). That installs MoveState("STUNNED", DizzyMove, StunIntent) with MustPerformOnce and FollowUpStateId defaulted to StateLog.Last() = HEADBUTT_MOVE (Creature.cs:530-543), so the rock spends one turn running DizzyMove (which clears IsOffBalance) and then headbutts again -- which means C#'s own POST_HEADBUTT -> DIZZY_MOVE arm is unreachable, a dead conditional arm in the shipped game. The sim drops the Stun call entirely (its _headbutt, bowlbugs.py:62-63, only attacks) and reaches the same lost turn through the POST_HEADBUTT conditional, with _dizzy clearing the flag (bowlbugs.py:65-66). Executed (monster_probes_b04.py rock-stun): a fully blocked headbutt leaves is_off_balance True and telegraphs DIZZY_MOVE; the next enemy side performs DIZZY, deals nothing, clears the flag and telegraphs HEADBUTT_MOVE -- the same turn-by-turn observable as the game, with the same StunIntent shown in between. The only residual difference is the StateLog, where C# ends with a duplicated HEADBUTT_MOVE and the sim with a DIZZY_MOVE entry; that is monster_state_machine G4's mechanism and it cannot bite here, because BowlbugRock has no RandomBranchState for the log to feed. G4 is not re-verdicted.

BowlbugRock.cs:36 HeadbuttDamage non-ascension = 15; sim _HEADBUTT_DMG = 15 (bowlbugs.py:24). It is a `public static` property in C# (read by BowlbugsWeak's preview) -- an accessibility detail with no behavioural content.

guards.what: ImbalancedPower is routed through the sim's on_damage_received rather than a dealer-side hook
guards.rationale: Recorded as a cross-tier observation, not a verdict on the power (rule 3: ImbalancedPower is the power tier's unit). C#'s trigger is AfterDamageGiven, which the killing-blow guard does NOT suppress; the sim's ImbalancedPower listens on `on_damage_received` (powers.py:2053-2072), which cmds.py:118-119 skips when the target died on that hit. For THIS monster the difference is unreachable by construction: the trigger requires WasFullyBlocked / amount == 0, and a fully blocked hit costs the target no HP, so it can never be the killing blow. Flagged to the power stream in the batch report.
